Subject: Production alert — sustained tail stalls on hosted API (16k/32k requests)

Jordan,

Quick heads up — over the last 90 minutes we've been seeing sustained tail stalls on Redwood hosted endpoints for large-context generations. This is impacting our customer-facing summarization pipeline (context sizes ~12–20k tokens).

Symptoms: 
- p95 latency moved from ~1.2s to ~2.1s for our workload (peak window 08:20–09:10 PST).
- p99 spikes to 7–9s and sometimes 12s for a small subset of long-context requests.
- Error rate (5xx) jumped from 0.3% baseline to ~6.8% during the same window.
- We observed an increase in rejected requests with HTTP 502/504. Sample request IDs attached.

We are on the hosted API (account: MED-9831, region: us-west-2). We need an urgent workaround — can you route our long-context requests to a fallback model or temporarily throttle large-window requests? Our client can also attempt chunking, but we need the server-side fallback while we test.

Attached: medialogic_spike_samples.tar.gz (logs), spike_request_ids.txt

Please loop in SRE and CS — this is customer-impacting for our production tenants.

Thanks,
Sarah Keane
Head of Ops, Medialogic

Thanks for the ping — quick technical read and proposed mitigations. I pulled the logs Jordan attached plus scheduler traces. High-level:

Findings: 
- A subset of long-context (>=12k) requests were being scheduled onto nodes with fragmented GPU memory after a sequence of quantized model deployments. Kernel memory maps show increased OOM-like allocation retries (not classical OOM, but allocation stalls).
- Autoscaler did not spin up new long-context workers fast enough due to pod-scheduler backpressure and a recent optimization that packs multiple small sessions onto high-memory nodes.
- The result: queueing at the runtime boundary leading to p99 amplification and some 502s when requests timed out waiting for runtime allocation.

Immediate mitigations (can implement within 1–3 hours):
1) Policy change: route MED-9831's long-context traffic to a separate capacity pool (model-redwood-16k-optimized) we can take out of packing. This reduces interference.
2) Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for sessions that reuse static prefixes (we can flip a config flag per-tenant).
3) Enforce soft cap of 16k on requested window size for hosted tier traffic from non-enterprise customers; route larger windows to a throttled queue with higher timeouts.
4) Deploy a quick scheduler patch to avoid placing long-context sessions on recently fragmented nodes (hot-pod avoidance).

I'll stand up a canary for routing (1) in us-west-2 and monitor. If we see immediate improvement, we can keep it and schedule a more thorough fix. ETA: canary in ~90 minutes, full mitigation in ~3 hours.

Attachments: runbook_long_context_fallback_v1.md (draft)

Dylan Brooks

Hi Sarah — thanks for sending the logs and the IDs. We're on it and appreciate the detailed traces — that made triage much faster.

Short-term customer-facing plan: 
- We're going to enable a per-tenant fallback that routes large-window requests to an optimized pool while we investigate. This should reduce queueing pressure quickly.
- Please add client-side chunking/retry (we can share a snippet) for any single request >12k tokens. Chunking reduces peak memory pressure and will help avoid retries.
- Can we schedule a 30-minute canary starting 12:30 PST where we run a controlled traffic replay? We need permission to replay a small subset of your production traces into our canary. That will help validate the fix before broad rollout.

We will also provide a temporary credit for the window of impact — Jordan and Neha are looped for the commercial side.
